what: Behind the panel a large wave plane (three.js, 90° field of view) lies tilted and paints three colors mixed by noise — vertices of the 400-cell grid are pushed 20 each forward/back and sideways by noise so the surface wrinkles, and color mixes c1·c2·c3 with slow noise (×.6) and twice-as-dense noise (×.4), then wraps the horizontal edges in c3. The clock travels along a circle that makes one turn per 180 seconds so it ripples endlessly, and at first it fades in from transparent with a 5s ease. When the color option changes, each frame moves .025 of the remaining difference toward the new color — a demo where pressing a swatch slowly bleeds the background color over, and a theme picker strip
ease: opacity 5s ease · color follows .025 per frame (at 60fps)

options.c1 · c2 · c3: Three colors (CSS colors or var(--x)) — default is dark blue, deep indigo and bright blue turned from the accent color. Editing the attribute flows to the new colors
options.speed: Share moved toward the new color each frame (0~1), default .025 — 0 changes at once
options.fade: Initial turn-on duration (sec), default 5 — 0 means instant
options.segments: Number of cells dividing the panel, default 400 (about 120 on light devices)

use: …

from.where: index.html .rk-play__bg (theme playground — clicking an accent swatch flows the three colors into that accent set)

note: three loads three.cjs after three-global.js as a regular <script> Loaded as such. On Android the original (React Three Fiber) drew a 136° two-color linear gradient switching over 1.5s instead of the shader — here the shader is drawn regardless of device, and without WebGL only the board’s background color remains. The noise function is not ported from the original but newly written as hash-gradient simplex
